article_title: Effectiveness evaluation of a serious game for dental lost wax casting training.
citation: Wang YiZhen, Li Yi, Ma ChaoYi, Zhang WeiYi, Yuan ZiYa, Zhu Qian, Zhao XiaoHan, Song Jinlin, Yang Sheng, Ji Ping, Pang MengWei. (2025). Effectiveness evaluation of a serious game for dental lost wax casting training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06643-8
title: D-Casting module: a free online serious game for lost-wax casting training and assessment
description: The D-Casting module is a free online application for lost-wax casting training for dental and dental technology students, delivered within the OMEDT system framework. It
requirements: an internet-accessible practice version and a separate exam version of the module, plus the accompanying material package
constraints: the article states the module excludes haptic simulation for psychomotor skill training and instead focuses on visual and reaction-based simulations
the study is limited to a single center, a specific domain (dental lost-wax casting) and a defined group of participants
target_learning_goals: familiarity with the lost-wax casting process and its steps
examples: the module constructs the entire casting process, including burnout, preparation of the centrifugal casting machine, melting, casting, and cooling, with multiple-choice and fill-in-the-blank selection elements and a reward/punishment mechanism

article_title: High acceptability of a newly developed urological practical skills training program.
citation: de Vries Anna H., van Luijk Scheltus J., Scherpbier Albert J. J. A., Hendrikx Ad J. M., Koldewijn Evert L., Wagner Cordula, Schout Barbara M. A. (2015). High acceptability of a newly developed urological practical skills training program. BMC Urology 15:93. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12894-015-0084-8
title: Dutch Urology Practical Skills (D-UPS) training program
description: The D-UPS program is a structured national skills curriculum for urology residents, designed with the backward design principle of Wiggins and McTighe and combining "the acquisition and rehearsal of basic theoretical knowledge ... with practical training of basic urological skills and techniques". It features mandatory one-hour weekly training sessions in the local hospital, starting with eight basic skills sessions (e.g. basic laparoscopy, flexible ureterorenoscopy) to be yearly repeated, each built from a Training Needs Analysis, an online formative test, supervised simulator training of procedural steps and pitfalls, peer teaching for seniors, and a closing evaluation.
requirements: Training needs analysis per session to identify procedural steps, pitfalls and learning objectives
Selection of a suitable simulator (Training Media Specification), with preference for low fidelity models to limit costs and simplify logistics
Structured scheduling of mandatory sessions in the local hospital
constraints: The article notes the Dutch situation limits generalizability, though the outline could serve as a blueprint for other surgical specialties and similar European residency programs
Validation of the curriculum is a multi-year process still pending at time of publication
target_learners: junior and senior urology residents in Dutch teaching hospitals
target_learning_goals: basic and advanced urological practical skills and techniques
non-technical skills and knowledge of instruments and procedural steps
examples: The first eight sessions include 'ultrasound of kidney and bladder', 'basic laparoscopy', 'electro surgery', 'mid urethral sling', 'transurethral resection of the prostrate' and 'flexible ureterorenoscopy'; laparoscopic tasks are derived from the validated European Basic Laparoscopic Urological Skills Exam
